BACKGROUND: NIST PSCR requires reinstalling and configuring an existing high-speed optical motion capture system that has been relocated. This system provides large-scale immersive virtual reality and indoor localization tracking. A ground-truth reference is essential for evaluating the capabilities and limitations of prototype indoor localization systems for public safety across large areas of a multistory building. The VR (VR) capabilities allow for tracking of multiple objects and individuals for testing communication technologies for first responders. The new system must be fully compatible with the existing OptiTrack cameras and Motive software currently in use at the laboratory. II. PURPOSE : The Public Safety Communications Research (PSCR) Division at NIST drives the development and implementation of critical communications technologies for the public safety community. B

The system shall enable dynamic control of the spatial phase and amplitude of laser beams to generate arbitrary illumina

high phase stability, and computer-controlled operation with software interfaces compatible with automated laboratory control. The system shall support operation over the wavelength range used for EOS measurements, including near-infrared telecommunications wavelengths, while maintaining high optical efficiency and low wavefront distortion. The SLM is required to support development of SI-traceable electro-optic waveform measurements, spatially resolved electric-field characterization, adaptive optical alignment, and precision optical beam engineering for advanced photonic, semiconductor, and ultrafast metrology applications. staffing_team.text: .docx ===== GENERAL INFORMATION CONTACT INFORMATION DESCRIPTION This requirement is being solicited under the authority of 38 U.S.C. 8153 and VAAR 873. Network Contracting Office 2 (NCO2), on behalf of the James J. Peters VA Medical Center (JJP VAMC) in the Bronx, NY, has a need for one Full-Time Equivalent (1.0 FTE) interventional radiology (IR) physician to provide onsite and on-call nonpersonal healthcare services to eligible beneficiaries of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA is anticipating procurement of these services from a contractor that can propose a minimum of four (4) board certified/board eligible IR physicians as key personnel to be credentialed & available for scheduling with JJP VAMC. The VA Radiology Services (and are accredited by ACR for Mammography) follow the standards of Abdominal/GU, Breast Imaging, Cardiovascular, General, Interventional, Musculoskeletal, Neuroradiology & guidelines set forth by American College of Radiology (ACR). A contractor providing IR services shall provide services that meet or exceed the American College of Radiology Guidelines https://www.acr.org/...IRClin-Prac-Mgmt. Network Contracting Office 2 (NCO2), on behalf of the James J. Peters VA Medical Center (JJP VAMC) in the Bronx, NY, has a need for one Full-Time Equivalent (1.0 FTE) interventional radiology (IR) physician to provide onsite and on-call nonpersonal healthcare services to eligible beneficiaries of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA is anticipating procurement of these services from a contractor that can propose a minimum of four (4) board certified/board eligible IR physicians as key personnel to be credentialed & available for scheduling with JJP VAMC. The VA Radiology Services (and are accredited by ACR for Mammography) follow the standards of Abdominal/GU, Breast Imaging, Cardiovascular, General, Interventional, Musculoskeletal, Neuroradiology & guidelines set forth by American College of Radiology (ACR). A contractor providing IR services sha

A contractor providing IR services shall provide services that meet or exceed the American College of Radiology Guidelines https://www.acr.org/...IRClin-Prac-Mgmt. The required number of hours to be on site is 2,080 (1.0 FTE). The estimated period of performance is one base year plus four one-year option periods.
